title: Needlebench: token pacing microprobe for p95 continuity and regression capture
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description: Build a lightweight, low-noise microprobe (Needlebench) that measures tokens/sec and latency tail (p95/p99) under steady-state and controlled drift scenarios for core models. This harness will be focused on deterministic, repeatable probes suitable for CI, nightly runs, and on-demand investigative runs. It should exercise realistic sequence length distributions, prefix cache warmups, and multi-tenant queueing artifacts so we can detect regressions in throughput and tail latency early.
acceptance_criteria: Needlebench can run headless in CI and produce JSON artifacts with per-second token-rate, p50/p95/p99 latencies, and histogram buckets compatible with our observability parser.
Detects >7% regression in tokens/sec or >15% regression in p95 relative to a golden baseline and emits a failing CI status with a link to regression artifact.
Supports configurable model variants, sequence-length distributions, batch sizes, and KV cache warmup policies via a single YAML manifest.
Runs end-to-end on hosted and dedicated environments and validates that fallback routing (cheapest/fastest) does not introduce unnoticed regressions.
Has a documented bisection flow to narrow down commits that introduced regression and a templated GitHub issue with diagnostic links.
Integrates with existing perf dashboard (PerfBoard) and uploads artifacts to s3 with immutable keys for historical comparisons.
plan: Prototype harness in Go to reuse existing low-level RPC client and heatmap exporters
Define canonical workloads: short-chat, long-form-compose, embedding-batches (map to token distributions)
Implement KV-cache warmup runner and an explicit cold-start runner so we can measure both steady-state and first-request latencies
Add per-second token counters and fixed-interval sampling for histogram buckets; push metrics to Prometheus and write JSON summary artifacts
Wire up CI job and nightly job; add regression detector script to compare against golden baseline stored in s3
Create runbook for bisect + alerting + required logs to triage (traces, model config, kernel selected, node telemetry)
Iterate on thresholds with SRE and ML infra to avoid false positives from noisy hardware changes
decisions: Language: Go for harness core (reuse existing RPC client). Python shim for CI orchestration & result parsing.
Metric plumbing: Prometheus histograms + JSON artifacts; PerfBoard will consume JSON daily uploads.
Failure criteria: absolute and relative checks to prevent tiny baseline noise from failing CI; initial default: >7% tokens/sec drop OR >15% p95 increase
KV-cache emulation: two-phase run (warmup with prefixes then measurement) configurable per workload
blockers: Need a stable test model image that mirrors production kernel selection (infra change scheduled in runtime-1.22).
Permissions for the CI runner to write to perf S3 bucket - security needs to approve IAM role (ticket SEC-1145).
